body:
### Problem

When the TUI goes away (terminal/tmux pane closed → SIGHUP), the `nvim --embed` server process that the TUI spawned does not exit if an error message is still pending (`did_emsg`): `getout()` calls `wait_return(false)` and blocks forever waiting for a keypress from a UI that no longer exists. The server is reparented to PID 1 and keeps running indefinitely, together with any `:terminal` jobs it owns.

Stack of a stuck server (macOS `sample`):

```
main → state_enter → input_get → inbuf_poll → loop_poll_events → multiqueue_process_events
  → exit_event → preserve_exit → getout → wait_return → vgetc → vgetorpeek → inchar
  → input_get → inbuf_poll → loop_poll_events → uv_run → kevent   (blocks forever)
```

`src/nvim/main.c` `getout()`:

```c
if (did_emsg) {
  // give the user a chance to read the (error) message
  no_wait_return = false;
  wait_return(false);
}
```

`wait_return()` only short-circuits with `if (headless_mode && !ui_active()) return;` (5b34c2a), so an `--embed` server whose UI has detached (not started with `--headless`) is not covered and blocks on `vgetc()`.

An easy way to get a pending error is `:wshada` when the ShaDa temp names `main.shada.tmp.a`…`.z` are all taken (#11955). Note that in the TUI this E138 is not even displayed (`:messages` is empty afterwards), yet it leaves `did_emsg` set, so the user has no hint that the next SIGHUP will strand the server.

On one machine here this had accumulated 132 orphan `nvim --embed` processes (each still holding its `:terminal` child) before we noticed.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $T/state/nvim/shada $T/cfg $T/data $T/cache
touch $T/state/nvim/shada/main.shada.tmp.{a..z}      # exhaust ShaDa temp names → :wshada fails with E138

tmux new-session -d -s repro -x 120 -y 30 \
  -e XDG_STATE_HOME=$T/state -e XDG_DATA_HOME=$T/data -e XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$T/cfg -e XDG_CACHE_HOME=$T/cache \
  "nvim -u NONE"
sleep 3
tmux send-keys -t repro ':wshada' Enter; sleep 1     # error is raised (did_emsg) but not shown
tmux kill-session -t repro                            # SIGHUP to the TUI and the server
sleep 4
ps -axo pid,ppid,command | grep '[n]vim --embed'      # server still alive, PPID 1
```

`sample <server pid>` shows the stack above. `kill -HUP <server pid>` directly (instead of killing the tmux session) reproduces as well. Without the pre-existing temp files (no E138) the server exits normally.

### Expected behavior

With no UI attached there is nobody to press Enter: `getout()` / `wait_return()` should not block, the error should go to stderr/log and the server should exit (as the `--headless` path already does).

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.12.5, Build type: Release, LuaJIT 2.1.1788856981 (Homebrew `neovim 0.12.5_1`). `wait_return()` / `getout()` on current master still have the same condition.

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A (Vim has no separate `--embed` server process).

### Operating system/version

macOS 27.0

### Terminal name/version

iTerm2 3.7.3 + tmux 3.7c

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-256color

### Installation

Homebrew
title: --embed server never exits after SIGHUP when an error message is pending: getout()→wait_return() blocks with no UI, leaving orphan nvim + :terminal jobs
